  PROBLEM: The matcher identifies the runner step-failure line by text and format rather than by source, so a passing step that prints `##[error]Process completed with exit code N` can be chosen as the anchor and hide the real failure.
  WHY: The scan stops at the first match, so the excerpt can omit a later genuine step failure, which is the defect the change was meant to fix. - scripts/collect_pr_check_runs_context.py:426-427, 437-439 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The matcher incorrectly assumes any log line matching the pattern `##[error]Process completed with exit code N` is the runner-generated step failure line.
  WHY: A passing test in a consumer workflow can print this text, and the matcher cannot tell it apart from the runner's line. The log excerpt then ends at that passing test line and cuts off the real error details, which reproduces the bug the change was meant to prevent.

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/collect_pr_check_runs_context.py:LOG_TAIL_STEP_FAILURE_LINE_RE (hunk @@ -41,6 +41,16 @@) and the matching loop in _select_log_tail_window | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The regex matches both the runner's real step-failure line and a passing test's stdout that prints the same text. The runner timestamps every stdout line, so the two are indistinguishable, and the loop anchors on the first hit.
  WHY: A passing step that emits runner-mimicking stdout before the real failing step's exit-code line gets the wrong anchor. The new tests test_non_step_failure_errors_fall_back_to_the_first_error and the timestamped STEP_ERROR case together show the matcher cannot tell the two sources apart.
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
